title: Batch API Pricing: When Async Jobs Save Money
description: Use provider batch discounts for work that can wait, while accounting for turnaround time, errors and repeat jobs.
tldr: Some providers offer lower rates for asynchronous batch processing. OpenAI documents a 50% Batch API discount for eligible work, but the benefit depends on successful completion and your workflow's latency needs.

sections.heading: Batch is a different workflow
sections.body: A batch job submits many independent requests and processes results later. It suits offline labeling, document extraction, evaluation and scheduled content processing. It is usually a poor fit for an interactive chat response that a person expects immediately.

sections.heading: Check the model and category
sections.body: OpenAI's Batch API documentation describes a 50% discount relative to standard synchronous API rates for eligible models and workloads. Other providers have their own batch rules. Check the current model, endpoint, turnaround window and pricing page before applying a blanket discount to all usage. Tool or non-text charges may follow different rules.

sections.heading: Example with a failure allowance
sections.body: If a standard text job would cost $100 and all requests qualify for a 50% batch discount, the ideal batch charge is $50. If 5% require a full-price retry, add roughly $5, giving about $55 before other costs. The exact amount depends on which requests failed and their token mix; track this from usage records.

sections.heading: Operational checklist
sections.body: Store a stable request ID for each item, validate outputs, and retry only failed items. Watch deadline and rate limits. If faster answers unlock revenue or prevent user abandonment, include that cost when deciding between synchronous and batch. [Estimate standard request cost](/tools/token-to-usd) before applying the provider's documented discount.

faq.question: Can every API request use batch pricing?
faq.answer: No. Eligibility depends on the provider, model and API endpoint, and batch results arrive asynchronously.

ctaText: Estimate your own usage with TokenRate tools, then compare with the provider's billing page.
